en.L: And Moab rebelled against Israel after the death of Ahab.
en.B: After Ahab died, Moab rebelled against Israel.
en.R: After Ahab died, the land of Moab rebelled against Israel and refused to be ruled by it any longer.

es.B: Después de la muerte de Acab, Moab se rebeló contra Israel.
es.R: Cuando murió Acab, el país de Moab se rebeló contra Israel y ya no quiso estar bajo su dominio.

fr.R: Après la mort d’Achab, le pays de Moab s’est révolté contre Israël et n’a plus voulu être sous son autorité.

vi.B: Sau khi A-háp qua đời, Mô-áp nổi loạn chống lại Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.R: Sau khi A-háp qua đời, xứ Mô-áp nổi dậy chống lại Y-sơ-ra-ên và không chịu để Y-sơ-ra-ên cai trị nữa.

ko.L: 그리고 아합이 죽은 뒤에 모압이 이스라엘에게 반역했다.
ko.B: 아합이 죽은 뒤에 모압이 이스라엘에게 반기를 들었다.
ko.R: 아합이 죽은 뒤에 모압 땅이 이스라엘에게 반역했다. 모압은 더 이상 이스라엘의 다스림을 받지 않으려고 했다.

decisions.choice: Moab rebelled: Moab threw off the rule of the kings of Israel
decisions.reason: Moab, east of the Dead Sea, had been made subject to Israel since David's day (2 Samuel 8:2), and its king paid a heavy yearly tribute in sheep and wool (3:4). The rebellion is told in full in 3:4-27. A Moabite inscription from this time, the stone of King Mesha, also tells of Moab breaking free from Israel.

decisions.choice: after the death of Ahab: the revolt came when a new king took the throne
decisions.reason: Ahab died in battle at Ramoth-gilead (1 Kings 22:34-37), and his son Ahaziah followed him (1 Kings 22:40, 52). A change of king was a natural moment for a subject people to break away. The verse stands alone here and is taken up again in 3:5.

decisions.choice: the land of Moab ... refused to be ruled by it any longer
decisions.reason: Readable explains what rebelling against Israel meant: Moab stopped accepting Israel's rule and paying its tribute (3:4-5).

decisions.choice: passé simple at Literal and Balanced; passé composé at Readable ("s’est révolté")
decisions.reason: For the whole block (2 Kings 1-12), as the French style guide and the Kings terms note: narration in the passé simple at L and B and in the passé composé at R; speech keeps spoken tenses at every level.

decisions.choice: "반기를 들었다" (raised the banner of revolt) at Balanced; "반역했다" at Literal and Readable
decisions.reason: "반기를 들다" is the usual Korean for a subject people throwing off a ruler; Literal keeps the plain verb "반역하다".

source.text: וַיִּפֹּ֨ל אֲחַזְיָ֜ה בְּעַ֣ד הַשְּׂבָכָ֗ה בַּעֲלִיָּת֛וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּשֹׁמְר֖וֹן וַיָּ֑חַל וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח מַלְאָכִ֔ים וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵהֶם֙ לְכ֣וּ דִרְשׁ֗וּ בְּבַ֤עַל זְבוּב֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י עֶקְר֔וֹן אִם־אֶחְיֶ֖ה מֵחֳלִ֥י זֶֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And fell Ahaziah through the lattice in his upper room which [was] in Samaria, and he became ill; and he sent messengers and said to them, go, inquire of Baal-zebub god of Ekron whether I will live from sickness this.

en.L: And Ahaziah fell through the lattice in his upper room that [was] in Samaria, and he became ill. And he sent messengers and said to them, "Go, inquire of Baal-zebub, [the] god of Ekron, whether I will live from this sickness."
en.B: Ahaziah fell through the lattice of his upper room in Samaria and was injured. So he sent messengers, telling them, "Go and consult Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron, whether I will get over this injury."
en.R: King Ahaziah fell through the wooden screen over a window in his upstairs room in Samaria, and he was badly hurt. He sent messengers and told them, "Go and ask Baal-zebub, the god of the city of Ekron, whether I will get well from this injury."

es.L: Y Ocozías cayó por la celosía de su aposento alto que [estaba] en Samaria, y enfermó; y envió mensajeros y les dijo: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}}, {{plural_you:consulten|consultad}} a Baal-zebub, dios de Ecrón, si viviré de esta enfermedad».
es.B: Ocozías se cayó por la celosía de su aposento alto en Samaria y quedó herido. Entonces envió mensajeros y les dijo: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} a consultar a Baal-zebub, el dios de Ecrón, si me recuperaré de esta herida».
es.R: El rey Ocozías se cayó por la reja de madera que cubría una ventana de su habitación en el piso de arriba, en Samaria, y quedó gravemente herido. Envió mensajeros y les dijo: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} y {{plural_you:pregunten|preguntad}} a Baal-zebub, el dios de la ciudad de Ecrón, si voy a sanar de esta herida».

fr.L: Et Achazia tomba par le treillis de sa chambre haute qui [était] à Samarie, et il fut malade. Et il envoya des messagers et leur dit : « Allez, consultez Baal-Zeboub, dieu d’Eqrôn, [pour savoir] si je vivrai [et sortirai] de cette maladie. »
fr.B: Achazia tomba par le treillis de sa chambre haute, à Samarie, et se blessa. Il envoya donc des messagers en leur disant : « Allez consulter Baal-Zeboub, le dieu d’Eqrôn, pour savoir si je me remettrai de cette blessure. »
fr.R: Le roi Achazia est tombé à travers le grillage en bois d’une fenêtre de sa chambre, à l’étage, à Samarie, et il a été gravement blessé. Il a envoyé des messagers en leur disant : « Allez demander à Baal-Zeboub, le dieu de la ville d’Eqrôn, si je vais guérir de cette blessure. »

sw.L: Na Ahazia akaanguka kupitia kimiani cha chumba chake cha juu kilichokuwa huko Samaria, akaugua. Akatuma wajumbe, akawaambia, "Nendeni, mkamwulize Baal-zebubu, mungu wa Ekroni, kama nitapona ugonjwa huu."
sw.B: Ahazia alianguka kupitia kimiani cha chumba chake cha ghorofani huko Samaria, akaumia. Basi akatuma wajumbe, akawaambia, "Nendeni mkamwulize Baal-zebubu, mungu wa Ekroni, kama nitapona jeraha hili."
sw.R: Mfalme Ahazia alianguka kupitia kiunzi cha mbao kilichofunika dirisha la chumba chake cha ghorofani huko Samaria, akaumia vibaya. Akatuma wajumbe, akawaambia, "Nendeni mkamwulize Baal-zebubu, mungu wa mji wa Ekroni, kama nitapona jeraha hili."

vi.L: A-cha-xia rơi qua song mắt cáo trong phòng cao của vua tại Sa-ma-ri, và vua lâm bệnh. Vua sai các sứ giả đi và bảo họ: "Hãy đi, cầu hỏi Ba-anh Xê-bụt, thần của Éc-rôn, xem ta có sống qua khỏi bệnh này không."
vi.B: A-cha-xia rơi qua song mắt cáo trên phòng cao của vua ở Sa-ma-ri và bị thương nặng. Vua sai sứ giả đi và dặn: "Hãy đi hỏi ý Ba-anh Xê-bụt, thần của Éc-rôn, xem ta có khỏi được vết thương này không."
vi.R: Vua A-cha-xia té xuyên qua tấm chắn bằng gỗ ở cửa sổ phòng trên lầu của vua tại Sa-ma-ri và bị thương nặng. Vua sai sứ giả đi và bảo họ: "Hãy đi hỏi Ba-anh Xê-bụt, thần của thành Éc-rôn, xem ta có lành bệnh không."

ko.L: 그리고 아하시야가 사마리아에 있는 그의 다락방의 격자창으로 떨어져 병이 들었다. 그리고 그가 사자들을 보내며 그들에게 말했다. "가서 에그론의 신 바알세붑에게 내가 이 병에서 살아날지 물어보아라."
ko.B: 아하시야가 사마리아에 있는 자기 다락방의 격자창 틈으로 떨어져 다쳤다. 그래서 그는 사자들을 보내며 일렀다. "가서 에그론의 신 바알세붑에게 내가 이 상처에서 회복될지 물어보아라."
ko.R: 아하시야 왕이 사마리아에 있는 자기 집 위층 방에서 창문을 가린 나무 창살을 뚫고 떨어져 크게 다쳤다. 그는 사자들을 보내며 말했다. "에그론 성읍에 가서 그곳 신 바알세붑에게 내가 이 상처에서 나을지 물어보아라."

decisions.choice: the lattice: a wooden grille or screen over an opening in the upper room
decisions.reason: The word is used of network or latticework (1 Kings 7:17). Here it is probably a wooden screen over a window or over an opening in the roof room, which gave shade and air. It gave way under the king's weight, and he fell to the floor below.

decisions.choice: Baal-zebub: "lord of flies", the name of a god worshiped at Ekron
alternatives: Baal-zebul, "Baal the prince", mocked as "lord of flies"
decisions.reason: The name joins Baal, "lord" or "owner", with a word for flies. It may name a god thought to send or drive away flies and the sickness they carry, or a god who gave oracles. Another possibility is that the original name was Baal-zebul, "Baal the prince" or "lord of the high house", and that Israel's writers changed one sound to make it mean "lord of flies" as a mockery. The evidence does not settle which is right.

decisions.choice: Baal-zebub and the Beelzebul of the Gospels
decisions.reason: In the Gospels Jesus' opponents call the ruler of the demons Beelzebul (Matthew 10:25; 12:24; Mark 3:22; Luke 11:15), a name that echoes this god of Ekron. Some later copies and translations of the Gospels spell it Beelzebub, as here.

decisions.choice: inquire of: ask a god for an oracle about the future
decisions.reason: Ekron was one of the five chief cities of the Philistines, on the coastal plain west of Judah (Joshua 13:3). To "inquire of" a god was to seek a word from it through a priest or prophet. Kings of Israel were to inquire of the LORD through his prophets (1 Kings 22:5-8), so Ahaziah's choice is a turning away from the God of his own land.

decisions.choice: became ill ... live from this sickness: injured by the fall, and asking whether he will survive
decisions.reason: The verb and noun are the usual words for being sick. Here the illness is the result of the fall, so the sense is "was hurt" and "will I recover from this injury". "Live" in such questions means to recover and survive (8:8).

decisions.choice: consult (Balanced); ask (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Inquire of" is kept at Literal. Balanced says "consult", and Readable "ask", which carry the sense of asking a god for an answer in plain words.

decisions.choice: King Ahaziah ... the wooden screen over a window ... the city of Ekron
decisions.reason: Readable names Ahaziah as king (1 Kings 22:52), describes the lattice, and says that Ekron was a city, since the bare words would not be clear to many readers.

decisions.choice: consultar a (Literal, Balanced); preguntar a (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Consultar a" is the ordinary Spanish for asking a god or a prophet for an answer and keeps the sense of seeking an oracle at Literal and Balanced; Readable says "preguntar", as the English says "ask".

decisions.choice: "Baal-Zeboub"
decisions.reason: The French transcription of the name, with "ou" for the Hebrew u as in the other names of these books; "Belzébuth" is the later Gospel form and is kept for the New Testament.

decisions.choice: "kumwuliza" (ask) at every level
alternatives: "kutafuta shauri kwa" (seek counsel from) at Balanced
decisions.reason: Swahili "kumwuliza" is the usual word for asking a god or a prophet for an answer and is plain enough for Readable, so one verb serves where English moves from "inquire of" to "consult" and "ask"; it is also the verb for inquiring of the LORD in Samuel.

decisions.choice: "Ba-anh Xê-bụt"
decisions.reason: The name keeps the Old Testament form built on "Ba-anh" (Baal) as the terms note spells it; the Gospels' "Bê-ên-xê-bun" is a later form of the name (m3).

decisions.choice: "cầu hỏi" (L); "hỏi ý" (B); "hỏi" (R)
decisions.reason: "Cầu hỏi" is the Samuel drafts' word for asking a god for an oracle; Balanced and Readable say it more plainly, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "바알세붑" for Baal-zebub and "에그론" for Ekron, the usual Protestant forms
decisions.reason: The Protestant Korean tradition spells the god's name "바알세붑"; the Gospels' "바알세불" is kept apart, as the English keeps Baal-zebub and Beelzebul apart (m3).

decisions.choice: The king gives his messengers orders in the plain style (해라체: "물어보아라")
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note: the king speaks 해라체 to his subjects.

source.text: וּמַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֗ה דִּבֶּר֙ אֶל־אֵלִיָּ֣ה הַתִּשְׁבִּ֔י ק֣וּם עֲלֵ֔ה לִקְרַ֖את מַלְאֲכֵ֣י מֶֽלֶךְ־שֹׁמְר֑וֹן וְדַבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵהֶ֔ם הַֽמִבְּלִ֤י אֵין־אֱלֹהִים֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אַתֶּם֙ הֹֽלְכִ֔ים לִדְרֹ֕שׁ בְּבַ֥עַל זְב֖וּב אֱלֹהֵ֥י עֶקְרֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] angel of Yahweh spoke to Elijah the Tishbite, arise, go up to meet [the] messengers of [the] king of Samaria, and speak to them, [is it] from without [there being] no God in Israel [that] you [are] going to inquire of Baal-zebub god of Ekron?

en.L: And the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Elijah the Tishbite, "Arise, go up to meet the messengers of the king of Samaria, and speak to them: 'Is it because there is no God in Israel [that] you [are] going to inquire of Baal-zebub, [the] god of Ekron?
en.B: But the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Elijah the Tishbite, "Get up and go to meet the messengers of the king of Samaria. Say to them, 'Are you going to consult Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron, because there is no God in Israel?
en.R: But the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Elijah the Tishbite, "Get up and go to meet the messengers the king of Samaria has sent. Ask them, 'Is there no God in Israel? Is that why you are on your way to ask Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron?

fr.B: Mais l’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} dit à Élie le Tishbite : « Lève-toi et va à la rencontre des messagers du roi de Samarie. Dis-leur : “Allez-vous consulter Baal-Zeboub, le dieu d’Eqrôn, parce qu’il n’y a pas de Dieu en Israël ?
fr.R: Mais l’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} a dit à Élie le Tishbite : « Lève-toi et va à la rencontre des messagers que le roi de Samarie a envoyés. Demande-leur : “Est-ce qu’il n’y a pas de Dieu en Israël ? Est-ce pour cela que vous allez interroger Baal-Zeboub, le dieu d’Eqrôn ?

sw.L: Na malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Eliya Mtishbi, "Inuka, panda uende kuwalaki wajumbe wa mfalme wa Samaria, ukawaambie, 'Je, ni kwa sababu hakuna Mungu katika Israeli hata mnakwenda kumwuliza Baal-zebubu, mungu wa Ekroni?
sw.B: Lakini malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimwambia Eliya Mtishbi, "Ondoka uende kuwalaki wajumbe wa mfalme wa Samaria. Uwaambie, 'Je, mnakwenda kumwuliza Baal-zebubu, mungu wa Ekroni, kwa sababu hakuna Mungu katika Israeli?
sw.R: Lakini malaika wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimwambia Eliya Mtishbi, "Ondoka uende kukutana na wajumbe waliotumwa na mfalme wa Samaria. Uwaulize, 'Je, hakuna Mungu katika Israeli? Ndiyo sababu mnakwenda kumwuliza Baal-zebubu, mungu wa Ekroni?

vi.L: Nhưng thiên sứ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với Ê-li người Thi-sê-be: "Hãy đứng dậy, đi lên gặp các sứ giả của vua Sa-ma-ri và nói với họ: 'Có phải vì không có Đức Chúa Trời trong Y-sơ-ra-ên mà các ngươi đi cầu hỏi Ba-anh Xê-bụt, thần của Éc-rôn sao?
vi.B: Nhưng thiên sứ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} bảo Ê-li người Thi-sê-be: "Hãy đứng dậy, đi đón các sứ giả của vua Sa-ma-ri và nói với họ: 'Các ngươi đi hỏi ý Ba-anh Xê-bụt, thần của Éc-rôn, có phải vì Y-sơ-ra-ên không có Đức Chúa Trời không?
vi.R: Nhưng thiên sứ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} bảo Ê-li người Thi-sê-be: "Hãy đứng dậy, đi đón các sứ giả mà vua Sa-ma-ri đã sai đi. Hãy hỏi họ: 'Y-sơ-ra-ên không có Đức Chúa Trời sao? Có phải vì thế mà các ngươi đi hỏi Ba-anh Xê-bụt, thần của Éc-rôn không?

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 천사가 디셉 사람 엘리야에게 말했다. "일어나 사마리아 왕의 사자들을 맞으러 올라가서 그들에게 말하여라. '이스라엘에 하나님이 없기 때문에 너희가 에그론의 신 바알세붑에게 물으러 가는 것이냐?
ko.B: 그러나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 천사가 디셉 사람 엘리야에게 말했다. "일어나 사마리아 왕의 사자들을 만나러 가서 그들에게 말하여라. '이스라엘에 하나님이 없어서 너희가 에그론의 신 바알세붑에게 물으러 가느냐?
ko.R: 그러나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 천사가 디셉 사람 엘리야에게 말했다. "일어나 사마리아 왕이 보낸 사자들을 만나러 가거라. 그리고 그들에게 물어라. '이스라엘에는 하나님이 안 계시냐? 그래서 너희가 에그론의 신 바알세붑에게 물으러 가는 것이냐?

decisions.choice: the angel of Yahweh ... the messengers of the king: one word, two senders
decisions.reason: The same Hebrew word means both "angel" and "messenger". The king sends his messengers to a foreign god, and Yahweh sends his own messenger to stop them. The angel of Yahweh speaks with Yahweh's authority, as in 1 Kings 19:5-7; who he is exactly is discussed at Judges 2:1 and 6:11.

decisions.choice: Elijah the Tishbite: the prophet from Tishbe in Gilead
decisions.reason: Elijah was introduced in 1 Kings 17:1 as from the settlers of Gilead, east of the Jordan. He had opposed Ahaziah's father Ahab and his worship of Baal (1 Kings 18; 21:17-29).

decisions.choice: is it because there is no God in Israel: a question that rebukes
decisions.reason: The question expects no answer. Israel has a God who can be asked, and he is Yahweh, the God who had just answered by fire on Mount Carmel (1 Kings 18:36-39). Seeking an answer from the god of a Philistine city treats Israel's God as if he were absent. The same question comes again in verses 6 and 16.

decisions.choice: the king of Samaria: the king of Israel, named by his capital
decisions.reason: Samaria was the capital of the northern kingdom, built by Omri (1 Kings 16:24). Calling Ahaziah "the king of Samaria" rather than "the king of Israel" may set him apart from the God of Israel he has turned from, as in 1 Kings 21:1.

decisions.choice: Are you going to ... because there is no God in Israel? (Balanced); Is there no God in Israel? Is that why ... (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the reason at the end of the question and Readable splits it into two short questions. Both keep it a question.

decisions.choice: el ángel del SEÑOR ... los mensajeros del rey
decisions.reason: Spanish has no single word for both senders, so the Hebrew word is "ángel" for the LORD's messenger and "mensajeros" for the king's, as in the English; the meaning decision explains the play.

decisions.choice: "malaika" for the angel of the LORD; "wajumbe" for the king's messengers
decisions.reason: Hebrew uses one word for both senders' messengers. Swahili has no word that covers both and still names a heavenly messenger, so it says "malaika" for the LORD's and "wajumbe" for the king's, as English says "angel" and "messengers"; the meaning note explains the play.

decisions.choice: Elijah's message calls the messengers "các ngươi"
decisions.reason: A prophet speaking God's rebuke to the king's men speaks with authority, as the king does to his servants.

decisions.choice: The angel of the LORD speaks to Elijah in the plain style (해라체), and the message Elijah is to give is in the plain style too
alternatives: the polite style for the message
decisions.reason: As the Korean style guide for God's words: the angel speaks for God, and the rebuke to the king's men keeps God's plain style.

decisions.choice: you will not come down from the bed you have gone up to: you will never get up from your sickbed
decisions.reason: Beds in a house of this kind could be raised above the floor, so a person "went up" onto a bed (Genesis 49:4; 1 Kings 17:19). Not coming down from it means dying there, without recovering.

decisions.choice: you will surely die: a doubled verb that makes the statement certain
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats the verb, "dying you will die", which makes it emphatic, as in Genesis 2:17. It is a sentence of judgment, not a prediction that could go either way.

decisions.choice: therefore: the sentence follows from the wrong just named
decisions.reason: "Therefore" links the judgment to the question of verse 3. Because the king turned to Baal-zebub, Yahweh gives the answer the king wanted, and it is death.

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD (Literal); the LORD says this (Balanced); this is what the LORD says (Readable)
decisions.reason: The prophetic formula keeps one wording at each level through Samuel, Kings and Chronicles. The LORD's words inside the speech are not set off with a further level of quotation marks.

decisions.choice: You will never get up from the bed you are lying on
decisions.reason: Readable states the meaning of the picture of going up onto and coming down from a bed.

decisions.choice: Así dice el SEÑOR (Literal); el SEÑOR dice esto (Balanced); esto es lo que dice el SEÑOR (Readable)
decisions.reason: The prophetic formula keeps the one wording per level used in the Spanish of Samuel, through Kings and Chronicles.

decisions.choice: Nunca te levantarás de la cama en la que estás acostado
decisions.reason: Readable states the meaning of the picture of going up onto and coming down from a bed, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "Ainsi parle le SEIGNEUR" (L); "le SEIGNEUR dit ceci" (B); "Voici ce que dit le SEIGNEUR" (R)
alternatives: "Ainsi parle le SEIGNEUR" at every level
decisions.reason: The messenger formula as in the French drafts of Samuel, one wording per level for the whole block.

decisions.choice: "BWANA asema hivi" (Literal); "hivi ndivyo BWANA asemavyo" (Balanced); "hili ndilo BWANA analosema" (Readable)
decisions.reason: The prophetic formula keeps one wording at each level through Kings, the wording of the Swahili 2 Samuel drafts. The same pattern is used when a messenger quotes the king (1:11).

decisions.choice: "CHÚA phán thế này" (L); "CHÚA phán như vầy" (B); "Đây là lời CHÚA phán" (R)
decisions.reason: The Samuel note's wording of the messenger formula, kept at each level through Kings; in the message God calls the king "ngươi".

decisions.choice: The messenger formula "이와 같이 말씀하신다" (L), "이렇게 말씀하신다" (B), "하시는 말씀은 이것이다" (R)
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note; Readable puts "this is what the LORD says" in plain words. The formula stays in the plain style here because the words are said to the king's messengers about the king.

decisions.choice: "침대에서 다시는 일어나지 못할 것이다" at Readable
decisions.reason: As the English Readable, the idiom is given its sense: he will never get up from his sickbed. Literal and Balanced keep "침상" and "내려오다".

source.text: וַיֹּאמְר֨וּ אֵלָ֜יו אִ֣ישׁ׀עָלָ֣ה לִקְרָאתֵ֗נוּ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלֵינוּ֮ לְכ֣וּ שׁוּבוּ֮ אֶל־הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אֲשֶׁר־שָׁלַ֣ח אֶתְכֶם֒ וְדִבַּרְתֶּ֣ם אֵלָ֗יו כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הַֽמִבְּלִ֤י אֵין־אֱלֹהִים֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אַתָּ֣ה שֹׁלֵ֔חַ לִדְרֹ֕שׁ בְּבַ֥עַל זְב֖וּב אֱלֹהֵ֣י עֶקְר֑וֹן לָ֠כֵן הַמִּטָּ֞ה אֲשֶׁר־עָלִ֥יתָ שָּׁ֛ם לֹֽא־תֵרֵ֥ד מִמֶּ֖נָּה כִּֽי־מ֥וֹת תָּמֽוּת׃

Therefore the bed which you have gone up there, not you will come down from it, for dying you will die.

en.L: And they said to him, "A man came up to meet us, and he said to us, 'Go, return to the king who sent you, and speak to him: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Is it because there is no God in Israel [that] you [are] sending to inquire of Baal-zebub, [the] god of Ekron? Therefore the bed that you have gone up on there, you will not come down from it, for you will surely die.'"
en.B: They told him, "A man came up to meet us. He said, 'Go back to the king who sent you and say to him, {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: Are you sending men to consult Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron, because there is no God in Israel? For that reason you will not come down from the bed you have gone up to; you will certainly die.'"
en.R: They answered, "A man came to meet us. He told us, 'Go back to the king who sent you. Tell him, This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: Is there no God in Israel? Is that why you are sending messengers to ask Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron? So you will never get up from the bed you are lying on. You are sure to die.'"

es.L: Y le dijeron: «Un hombre subió a nuestro encuentro y nos dijo: “{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}}, {{plural_you:vuelvan|volved}} al rey que {{plural_you:los|os}} envió y {{plural_you:díganle|decidle}}: Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: ¿Es porque no hay Dios en Israel que tú envías a consultar a Baal-zebub, dios de Ecrón? Por tanto, de la cama a la que has subido no bajarás, porque ciertamente morirás”».
es.B: Ellos le contestaron: «Un hombre subió a nuestro encuentro. Nos dijo: “{{plural_you:Vuelvan|Volved}} al rey que {{plural_you:los|os}} envió y {{plural_you:díganle|decidle}}: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto: ¿Envías hombres a consultar a Baal-zebub, el dios de Ecrón, porque no hay Dios en Israel? Por eso no bajarás de la cama a la que has subido; ciertamente morirás”».
es.R: Ellos respondieron: «Un hombre salió a nuestro encuentro. Nos dijo: “{{plural_you:Regresen|Regresad}} al rey que {{plural_you:los|os}} envió. {{plural_you:Díganle|Decidle}}: Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: ¿Acaso no hay Dios en Israel? ¿Por eso envías mensajeros a preguntarle a Baal-zebub, el dios de Ecrón? Por eso nunca te levantarás de la cama en la que estás acostado. Vas a morir sin remedio”».

fr.L: Et ils lui dirent : « Un homme est monté à notre rencontre et nous a dit : “Allez, retournez vers le roi qui vous a envoyés, et dites-lui : Ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Est-ce parce qu’il n’y a pas de Dieu en Israël [que] tu envoies consulter Baal-Zeboub, dieu d’Eqrôn ? C’est pourquoi le lit sur lequel tu es monté, tu n’en descendras pas, car tu mourras certainement.” »
fr.B: Ils lui répondirent : « Un homme est monté à notre rencontre. Il nous a dit : “Retournez vers le roi qui vous a envoyés et dites-lui : {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit ceci : Envoies-tu des hommes consulter Baal-Zeboub, le dieu d’Eqrôn, parce qu’il n’y a pas de Dieu en Israël ? Pour cette raison, tu ne descendras pas du lit où tu es monté ; tu mourras, c’est certain.” »
fr.R: Ils ont répondu : « Un homme est venu à notre rencontre. Il nous a dit : “Retournez vers le roi qui vous a envoyés. Dites-lui : Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Est-ce qu’il n’y a pas de Dieu en Israël ? Est-ce pour cela que tu envoies des messagers interroger Baal-Zeboub, le dieu d’Eqrôn ? Alors tu ne te relèveras jamais du lit où tu es couché. Tu vas mourir, c’est sûr.” »

Kwa hiyo kitanda ulichopanda juu yake, hutashuka kutoka kwake, kwa maana hakika utakufa.'"
sw.B: Wakamjibu, "Mtu mmoja alipanda kuja kutulaki. Akasema, 'Rudini kwa mfalme aliyewatuma, mkamwambie, Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asemavyo: Je, unatuma watu kwenda kumwuliza Baal-zebubu, mungu wa Ekroni, kwa sababu hakuna Mungu katika Israeli? Ndiyo sababu unatuma wajumbe kwenda kumwuliza Baal-zebubu, mungu wa Ekroni? Kwa hiyo hutainuka kamwe kutoka kitandani ulicholalia. Hakika utakufa.'"

Người ấy bảo: 'Hãy trở về với vua đã sai các ngươi và nói với vua: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán như vầy: Ngươi sai người đi hỏi ý Ba-anh Xê-bụt, thần của Éc-rôn, có phải vì Y-sơ-ra-ên không có Đức Chúa Trời không? Vì thế, ngươi sẽ không rời khỏi chiếc giường ngươi đã nằm lên; ngươi chắc chắn phải chết.'"
vi.R: Họ trả lời: "Có một người đến gặp chúng tôi. Người ấy bảo chúng tôi: 'Hãy trở về với vua đã sai các ngươi. Hãy nói với vua: Đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: Y-sơ-ra-ên không có Đức Chúa Trời sao? Có phải vì thế mà ngươi sai sứ giả đi hỏi Ba-anh Xê-bụt, thần của Éc-rôn không? Vì vậy, ngươi sẽ không bao giờ ra khỏi giường bệnh nữa. Chắc chắn ngươi sẽ chết.'"

ko.L: 그러자 그들이 그에게 말했다. "어떤 사람이 우리를 맞으러 올라와서 우리에게 말했습니다. '너희를 보낸 왕에게 돌아가서 그에게 말하여라. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다. 이스라엘에 하나님이 없기 때문에 네가 에그론의 신 바알세붑에게 물으려고 보내는 것이냐? 그러므로 네가 올라가 누운 그 침상에서 너는 내려오지 못할 것이다. 너는 반드시 죽을 것이다.'"
ko.B: 그들이 왕에게 대답했다. "어떤 사람이 우리를 만나러 올라와서 이렇게 말했습니다. '너희를 보낸 왕에게 돌아가서 말하여라. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다. 이스라엘에 하나님이 없어서 네가 에그론의 신 바알세붑에게 물으려고 사람들을 보내느냐? 그러므로 너는 올라가 누운 침상에서 내려오지 못하고, 반드시 죽을 것이다.'"
ko.R: 그들이 대답했다. "어떤 사람이 우리를 만나러 왔습니다. 그 사람이 우리에게 말했습니다. '너희를 보낸 왕에게 돌아가거라. 그리고 왕에게 말하여라. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀은 이것이다. 이스라엘에는 하나님이 안 계시냐? 그래서 네가 에그론의 신 바알세붑에게 물으려고 사자들을 보내느냐? 그러므로 너는 지금 누워 있는 침대에서 다시는 일어나지 못할 것이다. 너는 틀림없이 죽을 것이다.'"

decisions.choice: you are sending: the message now speaks to the king himself
decisions.reason: In verse 3 the question was put to the messengers, "you (plural) are going". In the words they bring back it is addressed to the king, "you (singular) are sending", because he is the one who sent them. Otherwise the message repeats verses 3-4.

decisions.choice: a man: the messengers do not know who he is
decisions.reason: The messengers call him only "a man". They obey him without knowing his name, which leads the king to ask what he looked like (verses 7-8).

decisions.choice: sending men (Balanced); sending messengers (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "sending" with no object; the messengers themselves are meant, as verse 16 says.

decisions.choice: The messengers report to the king in the formal polite style (합쇼체: "말했습니다"), and quote the man's words as he said them
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note for subjects speaking to the king.

en.L: And he said to them, "What [was] the manner of the man who came up to meet you and spoke these words to you?"
en.B: He asked them, "What kind of man was it who came up to meet you and told you these things?"
en.R: The king asked them, "What did the man look like who came to meet you and told you this?"

es.L: Y él les dijo: «¿Cuál [era] el aspecto del hombre que subió a {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} encuentro y {{plural_you:les|os}} habló estas palabras?».
es.B: Él les preguntó: «¿Qué clase de hombre era el que subió a {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} encuentro y {{plural_you:les|os}} dijo estas cosas?».
es.R: El rey les preguntó: «¿Cómo era el hombre que salió a {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} encuentro y {{plural_you:les|os}} dijo esto?».

fr.L: Et il leur dit : « Quelle [était] l’allure de l’homme qui est monté à votre rencontre et vous a dit ces paroles ? »
fr.B: Il leur demanda : « Quel genre d’homme était-ce, celui qui est monté à votre rencontre et vous a dit cela ? »
fr.R: Le roi leur a demandé : « À quoi ressemblait l’homme qui est venu à votre rencontre et qui vous a dit cela ? »

sw.B: Akawauliza, "Yule mtu aliyekuja kuwalaki na kuwaambia mambo haya alikuwa mtu wa namna gani?"
sw.R: Mfalme akawauliza, "Yule mtu aliyekuja kukutana nanyi na kuwaambia hivi alikuwa anaonekanaje?"

vi.B: Vua hỏi họ: "Người đã đi lên đón các ngươi và nói với các ngươi những điều ấy là người thế nào?"
vi.R: Vua hỏi họ: "Người đã đến gặp các ngươi và nói những điều ấy trông ra sao?"

ko.L: 그러자 그가 그들에게 말했다. "너희를 맞으러 올라와서 너희에게 이 말들을 한 그 사람의 모습이 [어떠하더냐]?"
ko.B: 왕이 그들에게 물었다. "너희를 만나러 올라와서 그런 말을 한 사람이 어떤 사람이더냐?"
ko.R: 왕이 그들에게 물었다. "너희를 만나러 와서 그 말을 한 사람이 어떻게 생겼더냐?"

decisions.choice: manner: what the man was like, his look and dress
decisions.reason: The word usually means "judgment" or "custom", and here the way something is, its fashion or appearance (Judges 13:12). The answer in verse 8 describes how he looked.

decisions.choice: What did the man look like
decisions.reason: Readable puts the question in the form the answer shows it to have.

en.B: They answered him, "He was a hairy man, with a leather belt tied around his waist." And the king said, "It is Elijah the Tishbite."
en.R: They answered, "He was a man with a lot of hair, and he wore a leather belt around his waist." The king said, "That was Elijah the Tishbite!"

es.L: Y le dijeron: «Un hombre dueño de pelo, y un cinturón de cuero ceñido a sus lomos». Y él dijo: «Elías el tisbita [es] él».
es.B: Ellos le respondieron: «Era un hombre velludo, con un cinturón de cuero atado a la cintura». Y el rey dijo: «Es Elías el tisbita».
es.R: Ellos respondieron: «Era un hombre con mucho pelo y llevaba un cinturón de cuero en la cintura». El rey dijo: «¡Era Elías el tisbita!».

fr.B: Ils lui répondirent : « C’était un homme velu, avec une ceinture de cuir serrée autour de la taille. » Et le roi dit : « C’est Élie le Tishbite. »
fr.R: Ils ont répondu : « C’était un homme avec beaucoup de poils, et il portait une ceinture de cuir autour de la taille. » Le roi a dit : « C’était Élie le Tishbite ! »

sw.B: Wakamjibu, "Alikuwa mtu mwenye nywele nyingi, naye amejifunga mshipi wa ngozi kiunoni." Mfalme akasema, "Huyo ni Eliya Mtishbi."
sw.R: Wakajibu, "Alikuwa mtu mwenye nywele nyingi, naye alivaa mshipi wa ngozi kiunoni." Mfalme akasema, "Huyo alikuwa Eliya Mtishbi!"

vi.L: Họ nói với vua: "[Là] một người có nhiều lông tóc, và có một dây thắt lưng bằng da buộc quanh hông." Vua nói: "Đó là Ê-li người Thi-sê-be."
vi.B: Họ thưa: "Đó là một người có nhiều lông tóc, lưng thắt dây da." Vua nói: "Chính là Ê-li người Thi-sê-be."
vi.R: Họ trả lời: "Người ấy có nhiều lông tóc, và thắt một dây lưng bằng da." Vua nói: "Đó là Ê-li người Thi-sê-be!"

ko.L: 그러자 그들이 그에게 말했다. "털이 많은 사람이었고, 허리에 가죽 띠를 띠고 있었습니다." 그러자 그가 말했다. "그는 디셉 사람 엘리야[이다]."
ko.B: 그들이 대답했다. "그는 털이 많은 사람이었고, 허리에 가죽 띠를 두르고 있었습니다." 그러자 왕이 말했다. "그는 디셉 사람 엘리야다."
ko.R: 그들이 대답했다. "그 사람은 털이 많았고, 허리에 가죽 띠를 두르고 있었습니다." 왕이 말했다. "그 사람은 디셉 사람 엘리야다!"

decisions.choice: an owner of hair: a hairy man
alternatives: a man wearing a garment of hair
decisions.reason: "Owner of" is a common Hebrew way of saying "having" something, so the phrase most simply means a man with much hair, on his head or body. It may instead describe his clothing: "a man with a garment of hair". Elijah's cloak is important in his story (1 Kings 19:13, 19; 2:8, 13 in this book), and Zechariah 13:4 speaks of prophets wearing a hairy cloak. Either way, the king recognizes him at once.

decisions.choice: a belt of leather girded on his loins: plain, rough clothing
decisions.reason: A leather belt was the simple dress of a poor man or a man of the open country, not the linen sash of the court. It marked Elijah as one who lived apart from the king's world.

decisions.choice: John the Baptist's dress echoes Elijah's
decisions.reason: The Gospels describe John the Baptist with a garment of camel's hair and a leather belt around his waist (Matthew 3:4; Mark 1:6), the description given here. Malachi 3:23 had promised that Elijah would come again, and Jesus says John fulfilled that promise (Matthew 11:14; 17:12-13).

decisions.choice: He was ... the king said
decisions.reason: The Hebrew answer is a string of descriptive words with no verb. Balanced and Readable make it a sentence, and name the king as the speaker of the reply.

decisions.choice: un hombre velludo
decisions.reason: Balanced follows the meaning decision, a hairy man, with the ordinary Spanish adjective; Literal keeps the Hebrew "dueño de pelo".

decisions.choice: "un homme velu"
decisions.reason: Balanced follows the meaning decision (a hairy man); Literal keeps the Hebrew "maître de poils" to show the idiom.

decisions.choice: "có nhiều lông tóc"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says the man was "an owner of hair"; Vietnamese "có nhiều lông tóc" keeps the plain sense of a hairy man (m1) without deciding whether a hair cloak is meant.

decisions.choice: "털이 많은 사람" at Literal for "an owner of hair"
decisions.reason: A word-for-word "owner of hair" is not Korean; the meaning decision gives the sense, a hairy man, which Korean says in a short phrase.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח אֵלָ֛יו שַׂר־חֲמִשִּׁ֖ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֑יו וַיַּ֣עַל אֵלָ֗יו וְהִנֵּה֙ יֹשֵׁב֙ עַל־רֹ֣אשׁ הָהָ֔ר וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלָ֔יו אִ֚ישׁ הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ דִּבֶּ֖ר רֵֽדָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he sent to him a commander of fifty and his fifty; and he went up to him, and behold, [he was] sitting on [the] top of the hill; and he spoke to him, man of God, the king has spoken, come down.

en.L: And he sent to him a commander of fifty and his fifty. And he went up to him, and look, he [was] sitting on the top of the hill. And he said to him, "Man of God, the king has spoken: Come down!"
en.B: Then the king sent a commander of fifty with his fifty men to Elijah. The commander went up to him, and there he was, sitting on top of the hill. He called to him, "Man of God, the king says, 'Come down!'"
en.R: Then the king sent a commander with his fifty soldiers to get Elijah. The commander climbed the hill where Elijah was sitting at the top. He said to him, "Man of God, the king orders you to come down!"

es.L: Y le envió un jefe de cincuenta y sus cincuenta. Y subió a él, y he aquí que [estaba] sentado en la cumbre del monte. Y le dijo: «Hombre de Dios, el rey ha dicho: ¡Baja!».
es.B: Entonces el rey envió a Elías un jefe de cincuenta con sus cincuenta hombres. El jefe subió hasta él, y allí estaba, sentado en la cumbre del monte. Le gritó: «Hombre de Dios, el rey dice: “¡Baja!”».
es.R: Entonces el rey envió a un jefe con sus cincuenta soldados a buscar a Elías. El jefe subió al monte, donde Elías estaba sentado en la cumbre, y le dijo: «Hombre de Dios, el rey te ordena que bajes».

fr.L: Et il envoya vers lui un chef de cinquante et ses cinquante. Et il monta vers lui, et voici, il [était] assis au sommet de la colline. Et il lui dit : « Homme de Dieu, le roi a parlé : Descends ! »
fr.B: Alors le roi envoya vers Élie un chef de cinquante hommes avec ses cinquante hommes. Le chef monta vers lui ; Élie était là, assis au sommet de la colline. Il lui cria : « Homme de Dieu, le roi dit : “Descends !” »
fr.R: Alors le roi a envoyé un officier avec ses cinquante soldats pour chercher Élie. L’officier a gravi la colline au sommet de laquelle Élie était assis. Il lui a dit : « Homme de Dieu, le roi t’ordonne de descendre ! »

sw.L: Akatuma kwake mkuu wa hamsini pamoja na hamsini wake. Akapanda kwake, na tazama, alikuwa ameketi juu ya kilele cha kilima. Akamwambia, "Mtu wa Mungu, mfalme amesema: Shuka!"
sw.B: Kisha mfalme alimtuma kwa Eliya mkuu wa kikosi cha watu hamsini pamoja na watu wake hamsini. Mkuu huyo akapanda kwake, akamkuta ameketi juu ya kilele cha kilima. Akamwita, "Mtu wa Mungu, mfalme anasema, 'Shuka!'"
sw.R: Kisha mfalme akamtuma kamanda mmoja pamoja na askari wake hamsini ili wamlete Eliya. Kamanda huyo akapanda kilima ambapo Eliya alikuwa ameketi kileleni. Akamwambia, "Mtu wa Mungu, mfalme anakuamuru ushuke!"

vi.L: Vua sai đến cùng Ê-li một viên chỉ huy năm mươi người cùng năm mươi người của ông ta. Viên chỉ huy đi lên gặp Ê-li, và kìa, Ê-li đang ngồi trên đỉnh đồi. Viên chỉ huy nói với Ê-li: "Hỡi người của Đức Chúa Trời, vua đã truyền: Hãy xuống đây!"
vi.B: Bấy giờ vua sai một viên chỉ huy năm mươi người dẫn năm mươi quân lính của mình đến gặp Ê-li. Viên chỉ huy đi lên, và thấy Ê-li đang ngồi trên đỉnh đồi. Ông ta gọi Ê-li: "Hỡi người của Đức Chúa Trời, vua truyền: 'Hãy xuống đây!'"
vi.R: Vua liền sai một viên chỉ huy dẫn năm mươi binh lính đi bắt Ê-li. Viên chỉ huy leo lên đồi, nơi Ê-li đang ngồi trên đỉnh. Ông ta nói với Ê-li: "Hỡi người của Đức Chúa Trời, vua ra lệnh cho ông xuống đây!"

ko.L: 그리고 그가 오십부장과 그의 오십 명을 그에게 보냈다. 그리고 그가 그에게 올라갔는데, 보라, 그가 산꼭대기에 앉아 있었다. 그러자 그가 그에게 말했다. "하나님의 사람이여, 왕께서 말씀하셨소. 내려오시오!"
ko.B: 그러자 왕이 오십부장과 그의 부하 오십 명을 엘리야에게 보냈다. 오십부장이 그에게 올라가 보니, 엘리야가 산꼭대기에 앉아 있었다. 그가 엘리야에게 말했다. "하나님의 사람이여, 왕께서 내려오라고 하시오!"
ko.R: 그러자 왕은 엘리야를 잡아 오려고 지휘관 한 사람을 군인 오십 명과 함께 보냈다. 지휘관은 엘리야가 앉아 있는 산꼭대기로 올라갔다. 그가 엘리야에게 말했다. "하나님의 사람이여, 왕께서 당신에게 내려오라고 명령하시오!"

decisions.choice: a commander of fifty and his fifty: an officer with the unit of soldiers he led
decisions.reason: Israel's army was organized in units of thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens (Exodus 18:21; 1 Samuel 8:12). Sending an armed unit shows that the king means to take Elijah by force.

decisions.choice: man of God: a prophet, one who belongs to God and speaks for him
decisions.reason: The title is used of Moses (Deuteronomy 33:1), of Samuel (1 Samuel 9:6) and of Elijah himself (1 Kings 17:18, 24). The commander uses it, yet in the same breath he orders the man of God about in the king's name.

decisions.choice: the king has spoken: come down
decisions.reason: The king's word is set against the word of Yahweh in verses 3-4. The king orders the prophet to come down; in verse 10 it is fire that comes down. The chapter turns on whose word has the power to do what it says.

decisions.choice: his fifty men (Balanced); his fifty soldiers (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "his fifty"; the men of his unit are meant. Literal keeps "his fifty". "Commander" follows the rule for a military officer (sar) in these books.

decisions.choice: there he was
decisions.reason: "Behold" points to what the commander saw. Balanced says "there he was"; Readable leaves it out and keeps the scene in its clause.

decisions.choice: un jefe de cincuenta y sus cincuenta (Literal); sus cincuenta hombres (Balanced); sus cincuenta soldados (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Jefe" is the word these books use for a military officer (sar), as "el jefe del ejército"; the men of his unit are supplied at Balanced and Readable, as in the English.

decisions.choice: "un chef de cinquante hommes" (B); "un officier avec ses cinquante soldats" (R)
decisions.reason: French names the rank plainly; Readable says "officier" for the commander, as the English Readable drops the "of fifty".

decisions.choice: "mkuu wa hamsini ... hamsini wake" (Literal); "mkuu wa kikosi cha watu hamsini" (Balanced); "kamanda ... askari wake hamsini" (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the bare "his fifty"; Balanced says that the officer led a unit of fifty men, and Readable uses the everyday "kamanda" and "askari". "Jemadari" is kept for the commander of a whole army, as in Samuel.

decisions.choice: "viên chỉ huy năm mươi người"
decisions.reason: The officer's title names the unit he led (m1); "viên chỉ huy" keeps him an officer of the king without a modern rank.

decisions.choice: "Hỡi người của Đức Chúa Trời"
decisions.reason: The first two commanders give an order in the king's name, so they call out with "hỡi" and no polite "thưa"; the third, who pleads, says "thưa ông" (verse 13).

decisions.choice: "오십부장" for "commander of fifty" at Literal and Balanced; "지휘관" at Readable
decisions.reason: "오십부장" is the established Korean title for an officer over fifty men; Readable says "a commander" with "fifty soldiers", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: The first two commanders speak to Elijah in the semi-formal 하오체 ("내려오시오"), an order passed on with little respect; the third pleads in 합쇼체 (verse 13)
decisions.reason: The commanders come to arrest the prophet in the king's name (m3); 하오체 lets Korean show the difference the story draws between them and the third commander, who kneels.

source.text: וַיַּעֲנֶ֣ה אֵלִיָּ֗הוּ וַיְדַבֵּר֮ אֶל־שַׂ֣ר הַחֲמִשִּׁים֒ וְאִם־אִ֤ישׁ אֱלֹהִים֙ אָ֔נִי תֵּ֤רֶד אֵשׁ֙ מִן־הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְתֹאכַ֥ל אֹתְךָ֖ וְאֶת־חֲמִשֶּׁ֑יךָ וַתֵּ֤רֶד אֵשׁ֙ מִן־הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַתֹּ֥אכַל אֹת֖וֹ וְאֶת־חֲמִשָּֽׁיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And answered Elijah and spoke to [the] commander of the fifty, and if [a] man of God [am] I, let come down fire from the heavens and let it consume you and your fifty; and came down fire from the heavens and consumed him and his fifty.

en.L: And Elijah answered and said to the commander of the fifty, "And if I [am] a man of God, let fire come down from the heavens and consume you and your fifty." And fire came down from the heavens and consumed him and his fifty.
en.B: Elijah answered the commander of the fifty, "If I am a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and devour you and your fifty men!" Then fire came down from heaven and consumed him and his fifty men.
en.R: Elijah answered the commander, "If I really am a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and burn you up along with your fifty soldiers!" Then fire came down from heaven and burned up the commander and his fifty soldiers.

es.L: Y respondió Elías y dijo al jefe de los cincuenta: «Y si yo [soy] hombre de Dios, que descienda fuego de los cielos y te consuma a ti y a tus cincuenta». Y descendió fuego de los cielos y lo consumió a él y a sus cincuenta.
es.B: Elías respondió al jefe de los cincuenta: «Si soy hombre de Dios, ¡que baje fuego del cielo y te devore a ti y a tus cincuenta hombres!». Y bajó fuego del cielo y lo consumió a él y a sus cincuenta hombres.
es.R: Elías le respondió al jefe: «Si de verdad soy hombre de Dios, ¡que baje fuego del cielo y te queme a ti junto con tus cincuenta soldados!». Entonces bajó fuego del cielo y quemó al jefe y a sus cincuenta soldados.

fr.L: Et Élie répondit et dit au chef de cinquante : « Eh bien, si je [suis] un homme de Dieu, que le feu descende des cieux et te dévore, toi et tes cinquante. » Et le feu descendit des cieux et le dévora, lui et ses cinquante.
fr.B: Élie répondit au chef de cinquante : « Si je suis un homme de Dieu, que le feu descende du ciel et te dévore, toi et tes cinquante hommes ! » Alors le feu descendit du ciel et le consuma, lui et ses cinquante hommes.
fr.R: Élie a répondu à l’officier : « Si je suis vraiment un homme de Dieu, que le feu descende du ciel et te brûle, toi et tes cinquante soldats ! » Alors le feu est descendu du ciel et a brûlé l’officier et ses cinquante soldats.

sw.L: Eliya akajibu, akamwambia mkuu wa hamsini, "Ikiwa mimi [ni] mtu wa Mungu, moto na ushuke kutoka mbinguni ukuteketeze wewe na hamsini wako." Moto ukashuka kutoka mbinguni, ukamteketeza yeye na hamsini wake.
sw.B: Eliya akamjibu yule mkuu wa hamsini, "Ikiwa mimi ni mtu wa Mungu, moto na ushuke kutoka mbinguni ukumeze wewe na watu wako hamsini!" Ndipo moto ukashuka kutoka mbinguni, ukamteketeza yeye na watu wake hamsini.
sw.R: Eliya akamjibu kamanda, "Ikiwa kweli mimi ni mtu wa Mungu, moto na ushuke kutoka mbinguni ukuteketeze wewe pamoja na askari wako hamsini!" Ndipo moto ukashuka kutoka mbinguni, ukamteketeza kamanda pamoja na askari wake hamsini.

vi.L: Ê-li đáp lời viên chỉ huy năm mươi người: "Nếu ta là người của Đức Chúa Trời, thì hãy để lửa từ trời xuống thiêu nuốt ngươi và năm mươi người của ngươi." Lửa từ trời xuống thiêu nuốt viên chỉ huy và năm mươi người của ông ta.
vi.B: Ê-li trả lời viên chỉ huy năm mươi người: "Nếu ta là người của Đức Chúa Trời, nguyện lửa từ trời xuống thiêu nuốt ngươi và năm mươi quân lính của ngươi!" Lập tức lửa từ trời giáng xuống thiêu đốt viên chỉ huy cùng năm mươi quân lính của ông ta.
vi.R: Ê-li trả lời viên chỉ huy: "Nếu ta thật là người của Đức Chúa Trời, thì nguyện lửa từ trời xuống thiêu rụi ngươi cùng năm mươi binh lính của ngươi!" Lửa liền từ trời xuống thiêu rụi viên chỉ huy và năm mươi binh lính của ông ta.

ko.L: 그러자 엘리야가 대답하여 오십부장에게 말했다. "내가 하나님의 사람이라면, 하늘에서 불이 내려와 너와 너의 오십 명을 삼킬 것이다." 그러자 하늘에서 불이 내려와 그와 그의 오십 명을 삼켰다.
ko.B: 엘리야가 오십부장에게 대답했다. "내가 하나님의 사람이라면, 하늘에서 불이 내려와 너와 네 부하 오십 명을 삼켜 버릴 것이다!" 그러자 하늘에서 불이 내려와 그와 그의 부하 오십 명을 태워 버렸다.
ko.R: 엘리야가 지휘관에게 대답했다. "내가 정말 하나님의 사람이라면, 하늘에서 불이 내려와 너와 네 군인 오십 명을 태워 버릴 것이다!" 그러자 하늘에서 불이 내려와 지휘관과 군인 오십 명을 태워 버렸다.

decisions.choice: if I am a man of God ... let fire come down: a word play on man and fire
decisions.reason: In Hebrew "man" (*'ish*) and "fire" (*'esh*) sound almost alike, and "come down" picks up the king's order in verse 9. The king told the man of God to come down; instead fire comes down. The answer shows that Elijah is indeed what the commander called him.

decisions.choice: fire from heaven: as at Mount Carmel
decisions.reason: Fire from Yahweh had come down on Elijah's sacrifice on Mount Carmel (1 Kings 18:38) to show who is God in Israel. Here it falls on those sent against his prophet. In Luke 9:54 James and John ask Jesus whether they should call down fire from heaven on a village that would not receive him, and Jesus rebukes them.

decisions.choice: consume: burn up completely
decisions.reason: The verb means "eat", and is used of fire that destroys what it touches (Leviticus 9:24; 1 Kings 18:38).

decisions.choice: your fifty men, his fifty men (Balanced); fifty soldiers (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 9.

decisions.choice: devour (in Elijah's words); consumed (in the narrative)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb is the same, "eat". Balanced uses the vivid "devour" in Elijah's spoken curse and the plainer "consumed" for what happened; both mean that the fire destroyed them completely. Verse 12 follows the same pattern.

decisions.choice: devore (in Elijah's words); consumió (in the narrative)
decisions.reason: As in the English Balanced, the one Hebrew verb is the vivid "devorar" in Elijah's curse and the plainer "consumir" for what happened.

decisions.choice: Elijah answers the commanders with "ta" and "ngươi"
decisions.reason: The prophet answers a summons given in the king's name with the same authority; to the humble third commander he says nothing in this form.

decisions.choice: Elijah answers the commanders in the plain style (해라체, "너")
decisions.reason: The prophet answers men sent to arrest him with the authority of God's spokesman; the plain style carries that.

decisions.choice: The wish "let fire come down" is said as a certainty, "불이 내려와 ... 삼킬 것이다"
decisions.reason: Korean has no third-person jussive that is not archaic; a plain future keeps the force of Elijah's words without the old "-ㄹ지어다".

source.text: וַיָּ֜שָׁב וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח אֵלָ֛יו שַׂר־חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים אַחֵ֖ר וַחֲמִשָּׁ֑יו וַיַּ֨עַן֙ וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלָ֔יו אִ֚ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים כֹּֽה־אָמַ֥ר הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ מְהֵרָ֥ה רֵֽדָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he again sent to him [a] commander of fifty, another, and his fifty; and he answered and spoke to him, man of God, thus says the king, quickly come down.

en.L: And he again sent to him another commander of fifty and his fifty. And he answered and said to him, "Man of God, thus says the king: Come down quickly!"
en.B: The king sent to him another commander of fifty with his fifty men. This one spoke up and said to him, "Man of God, the king says this: Come down at once!"
en.R: So the king sent another commander with his fifty soldiers. This commander said to Elijah, "Man of God, this is what the king says: Come down right now!"

es.L: Y volvió a enviarle otro jefe de cincuenta y sus cincuenta. Y este respondió y le dijo: «Hombre de Dios, así dice el rey: ¡Baja pronto!».
es.B: El rey le envió otro jefe de cincuenta con sus cincuenta hombres. Este tomó la palabra y le dijo: «Hombre de Dios, el rey dice esto: ¡Baja enseguida!».
es.R: Entonces el rey envió a otro jefe con sus cincuenta soldados. Este jefe le dijo a Elías: «Hombre de Dios, esto es lo que dice el rey: ¡Baja ahora mismo!».

fr.L: Et il lui envoya de nouveau un autre chef de cinquante et ses cinquante. Et il prit la parole et lui dit : « Homme de Dieu, ainsi parle le roi : Descends vite ! »
fr.B: Le roi lui envoya encore un autre chef de cinquante avec ses cinquante hommes. Celui-ci prit la parole et lui dit : « Homme de Dieu, le roi dit ceci : Descends tout de suite ! »
fr.R: Alors le roi a envoyé un autre officier avec ses cinquante soldats. Cet officier a dit à Élie : « Homme de Dieu, voici ce que dit le roi : Descends immédiatement ! »

sw.L: Akamtuma tena kwake mkuu mwingine wa hamsini pamoja na hamsini wake. Akajibu, akamwambia, "Mtu wa Mungu, mfalme asema hivi: Shuka upesi!"
sw.B: Mfalme alimtuma kwake mkuu mwingine wa kikosi cha watu hamsini pamoja na watu wake hamsini. Huyu naye akasema, "Mtu wa Mungu, hivi ndivyo mfalme asemavyo: Shuka mara moja!"
sw.R: Basi mfalme akamtuma kamanda mwingine pamoja na askari wake hamsini. Kamanda huyo akamwambia Eliya, "Mtu wa Mungu, hili ndilo mfalme analosema: Shuka sasa hivi!"

vi.L: Vua lại sai đến cùng Ê-li một viên chỉ huy năm mươi người khác cùng năm mươi người của ông ta. Viên chỉ huy lên tiếng nói với Ê-li: "Hỡi người của Đức Chúa Trời, vua phán thế này: Hãy mau xuống đây!"
vi.B: Vua lại sai một viên chỉ huy năm mươi người khác dẫn năm mươi quân lính của mình đến gặp Ê-li. Người này lên tiếng nói với Ê-li: "Hỡi người của Đức Chúa Trời, vua truyền như vầy: Hãy xuống ngay!"
vi.R: Vua lại sai một viên chỉ huy khác dẫn năm mươi binh lính đến. Viên chỉ huy này nói với Ê-li: "Hỡi người của Đức Chúa Trời, đây là lệnh vua: Hãy xuống ngay lập tức!"

ko.L: 그리고 그가 다시 다른 오십부장과 그의 오십 명을 그에게 보냈다. 그러자 그가 대답하여 그에게 말했다. "하나님의 사람이여, 왕께서 이와 같이 말씀하시오. 빨리 내려오시오!"
ko.B: 왕이 다시 다른 오십부장과 그의 부하 오십 명을 엘리야에게 보냈다. 이 사람도 엘리야에게 말했다. "하나님의 사람이여, 왕께서 이렇게 말씀하시오. 당장 내려오시오!"
ko.R: 그러자 왕은 다른 지휘관을 군인 오십 명과 함께 또 보냈다. 이 지휘관이 엘리야에게 말했다. "하나님의 사람이여, 왕께서 하시는 말씀이오. 지금 당장 내려오시오!"

decisions.choice: he answered: the Hebrew text as it stands
decisions.reason: Where verses 9 and 13 say the commander "went up", the Hebrew here says he "answered", meaning he spoke up, since no one has spoken to him. The two verbs differ by one letter, and the Greek translation reads "went up" here. The Hebrew text is followed, in the sense "spoke up".

decisions.choice: thus says the king: the commander speaks as if the king were God
decisions.reason: The second commander uses the very formula a prophet uses for Yahweh's word, "thus says", and adds "quickly". His order is harsher than the first, and it claims for the king the authority that belongs to Yahweh.

decisions.choice: he again sent: the king repeats what he did
decisions.reason: "Returned and sent" is a Hebrew way of saying "sent again". The king does not learn from the first disaster.

decisions.choice: the king says this (Balanced); this is what the king says (Readable)
decisions.reason: The commander's formula is put in the same words each level uses for "thus says the LORD" (verse 4), so the reader can hear the claim it makes.

decisions.choice: así dice el rey; el rey dice esto; esto es lo que dice el rey
decisions.reason: The commander's words take the same wording at each level as "Así dice el SEÑOR" (verse 4), so that the reader can hear the claim he makes.

decisions.choice: "vua phán thế này"
decisions.reason: The commander uses the messenger formula of the prophets for the king's order (m2); Literal keeps the echo of "CHÚA phán thế này" with the same verb.

decisions.choice: The commander uses the prophets' formula for the king: "왕께서 이와 같이 말씀하시오" (L), "이렇게 말씀하시오" (B)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision notes that he speaks as if the king were God; keeping the same formula as for the LORD shows it in Korean too.
